topic.name: On the Grasshopper and Cricket
topic.description: Keats's sonnet is a nature poem, not a story -- the grasshopper and cricket are symbols of an unending song of the earth, one carrying it through summer, the other through winter.

concepts.name: John Keats, the poet
concepts.description: The poem is signed with its poet's name directly beneath the second stanza.
concepts.definition: The poem 'On the Grasshopper and Cricket' is written by John Keats.

concepts.name: The poetry of earth is never dead
concepts.description: The first stanza opens with the claim that the poetry of earth is never dead, even when the birds fall faint in the heat and hide in cooling trees.
concepts.definition: The poetry of earth is never dead.

concepts.name: The poetry of earth is ceasing never
concepts.description: The second stanza opens with the matching claim for winter -- the poetry of earth is ceasing never, even on a lone winter evening when frost has brought silence.
concepts.definition: The poetry of earth is ceasing never.

concepts.name: Birds faint with the hot sun
concepts.description: In the first stanza, when all the birds are faint with the hot sun, they hide in cooling trees -- the moment the grasshopper's voice takes over.
concepts.definition: When all the birds are faint with the hot sun, and hide in cooling trees, a voice will run from hedge to hedge.

concepts.name: The grasshopper's summer luxury
concepts.description: The grasshopper takes the lead in summer, never done with his delights, and when tired out he rests at ease beneath some pleasant weed.
concepts.definition: That is the grasshopper's; he takes the lead in summer luxury, and when tired he rests at ease beneath some pleasant weed.

concepts.name: The cricket's song through the frost
concepts.description: On a lone winter evening, when the frost has brought a silence, the cricket's song shrills loud and clear from the stone, its warmth ever increasing.
concepts.definition: The frost has wrought a silence, from the stone there shrills the cricket's song, in warmth increasing ever.
